prerequisites: It is recommended to have previously studied Fundamentos de teoría de circuitos y máquinas eléctricas (Fundamentals of Circuit Theory and Electrical Machines).
It is recommended to have previously studied Electrotecnia aplicada (Applied Electrotechnics).
It is required to have passed or be currently enrolled in all subjects from academic years prior to the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Transmit basic innovative concepts related to the incorporation of electrical components in vehicles.
Offer students a vision of the technological evolution and future challenges concerning electrical components and different onboard electrical network solutions in vehicles.
Clarify the operating characteristics of different electrical components, as well as the various configurations of the electrical installation in automobiles.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Vehicle types. History of electric vehicles. Future prospects.
Introduction. Electrical installation. Electrical diagrams. Location of electrical components in the electrical diagram. Main circuits composing the electrical diagram.
Introduction. Main electrical systems. Auxiliary electrical systems. Actuation. Traction. Auxiliary devices. Onboard equipment. Sensors.
Introduction. Requirements for electric traction. Types of electric traction motors. Control and actuation. Applications.
Introduction. Communication systems: Elements; Configurations; Buses. Control systems: Static; Dynamic; Safety; Motor.
Introduction. Batteries. Fuel cells. Supercapacitors. Flywheel. Trends. Integration into the electrical grid.
Introduction. Charging modes. Connector types. Support infrastructure. Types of power supply networks. Alternative energies. Architecture of a charge manager. Smart grids.
Laboratory practices: Approach to different electrical components, their analysis and identification.
assessment_rules: The student can choose between two evaluation options: Option A (Global Evaluation) or Option B (Continuous Evaluation). Option A is a single written exam, requiring 5/10 or higher to pass. Option B involves written reports (60%) and presentations (40%), needing minimums of 2.4/10 and 1.6/10 respectively, and an overall score of 5/10 or higher. Failure to meet Option B's component minimums results in a 3/10 final grade, while non-ethical behavior leads to a 0.00 failing grade.
